findings.title: All WARN-tier token-economy hooks emit on a channel the model never receives (stderr + exit 0) — 4 guards are silent no-ops [CONFIRMED]
findings.mechanism: cascade-read-check (P1-CASCADE/KIT-011), context-budget-warn (KIT-018), docs-staleness-check (S64 operator WARN decision), pertask-state-warn (KIT-013) all print warnings to stderr and exit 0. Per Claude Code hook semantics, PreToolUse stderr is fed to the model ONLY on blocking exit 2; UserPromptSubmit injects STDOUT (not stderr) into context on exit 0. So the agent that is supposed to change behavior (use offset/limit, run /compact, update docs/SPRINT_STATE) never sees the warning.
findings.evidence: (1) kit/hooks/lib/cascade_check.py:41 `file=sys.stderr` + wrapper kit/hooks/cascade-read-check.sh:12-13 `|| true; exit 0`. (2) kit/hooks/context-budget-warn.sh:54-63 all `>&2`, :66 `exit 0` (UserPromptSubmit — stdout would be injected, stderr is not). (3) kit/hooks/docs-staleness-check.sh:103 `cat >&2`, :121 `exit 0`. (4) kit/hooks/pertask-state-warn.sh:37 `cat >&2`, :42 `exit 0`. (5) Live reproduction this session: `cat llm-wiki/wiki/log.md > /dev/null` (exact banned-file trigger) returned only my own echo — no WARN in tool result; manual invocation of the hook with the identical JSON payload prints '⚠️ CASCADE-WARN: cat/less крупного файла .../log.md (~240КБ > 50КБ)' and exit 0 — hook fires, output dropped. (6) Scan of ~143MB jsonl (all sessions in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-Apple-Desktop-Vibe-Code-Bot-AI-Traiding-Bot/): 0 organically rendered WARNs; the only rendered 'Context warning: transcript 900KB'/'Context URGENT: transcript 1300KB' strings are a manual hook test dated 2026-04-26T23:47Z ('=== test 900KB file (yellow warn) ===') and doc-page echoes — despite sessions provably exceeding 800/1000KB thresholds on every prompt (61 autocompactions, transcripts to 126MB) since the hook was installed. (7) Brief item (a) answered: banned-file full-reads post-hook (S62, 2026-07-02) = 0; pre-hook = 8 in main session (6× log.md incl. worktree copies, Apr 20-23) — but the guard as built could not have prevented recurrence anyway.
findings.why_weak: Four token-economy guarantees the kit lists as shipped (S59/S62/S64) are decorative: the S64 operator decision 'docs/=WARN — пуш НЕ блокируется, реши осознанно' presumes the agent sees the warning to decide consciously; it cannot. In fully autonomous runs (auto-resume, mega-run) even the human-terminal fallback is absent.
findings.proposed_direction: One-line channel fix per hook: context-budget-warn → print to stdout (UserPromptSubmit stdout is context-injected at exit 0); the three PreToolUse warns → emit JSON `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"allow","additionalContext":"<warn text>"}}` on stdout. Add a regression case to kit/hooks/tests asserting the warn text actually reaches tool-result/context (red/green via real hook invocation, per hook-test discipline).
findings.verify_note: Finding CONFIRMED — every element of the cited evidence reproduces independently, and no refutation criterion applies. (1) Code: all four hooks emit warnings to stderr and exit 0 — kit/hooks/lib/cascade_check.py:42 `file=sys.stderr` with wrapper cascade-read-check.sh:12-13 `|| true; exit 0`; context-budget-warn.sh:54-63 all `>&2`, :66 `exit 0`; docs-staleness-check.sh:103 `cat >&2`, :121 `exit 0`; pertask-state-warn.sh:37 `cat >&2`, :42 `exit 0`. (2) Registration: the three warn hooks are PreToolUse (Bash/Read matchers), context-budget-warn is UserPromptSubmit — in BOTH kit/settings.example.json and live ~/.claude/settings.json; per documented hook semantics PreToolUse stderr reaches the model only on exit 2, and UserPromptSubmit injects stdout (not stderr) at exit 0, so the channel claim is correct. (3) Live reproduction this session: real `cat llm-wiki/wiki/log.md > /dev/null && echo MARKER` returned ONLY my marker — no WARN in tool result; manual invocation of ~/.claude/hooks/cascade-read-check.sh with the identical JSON payload printed the exact CASCADE-WARN (~240КБ) to stderr with empty stdout, exit 0 — hook fires, output dropped before reaching the model. (4) Transcript scan reproduces: the only jsonl containing CASCADE-WARN / "Docs staleness WARN" / "Per-task protocol (KIT-013)" is the CURRENT session (67b1586c — my own manual invocation and Read echoes of hook source); the only "Context warning: transcript 900KB" render is a manual hook test tool_result timestamped 2026-04-26T23:47:11Z ("=== test 900KB file (yellow warn) ===") plus a script-source echo in d61d6e5e — despite transcripts of 123.5MB/15.7MB/5.3MB/1.39MB/1.27MB (far past the 800/1200KB thresholds, meaning the budget hook fired on every prompt) and 63 autocompactions. Zero organic warn deliveries ever. (5) Not fixed in S57-S67: live ~/.claude/hooks copies are byte-identical to repo kit/hooks at alpha.67; zero uses of hookSpecificOutput/additionalContext anywhere in kit/, .claude/, llm-wiki/. (6) Not already tracked: grep of UNIFIED-BACKLOG-S57.md, kit-op-detect-hardening-backlog.md, components/error-taxonomy.md finds no stderr/channel/warn-visibility item. (7) No operator-decision contradiction: S64 "docs/=WARN — реши осознанно" presumes the warning reaches the decision-maker; the proposed fix preserves WARN-not-block policy and only corrects the channel. Minor mitigating notes (do not refute): context-budget-hook.md documents intent as "warning visible к operator" (operator-facing by design, and autocompact provides a backstop), and post-S62 banned-file full reads = 0 so cascade-warn had no missed save yet — but the three PreToolUse warns textually instruct the AGENT ("Читай через offset+limit", "Обнови страницы через docs-update", "обновлять SPRINT_STATE после каждой задачи"), and in autonomous runs (auto-resume, claude -p mega-run) no human terminal exists at all.

(1) Evidence reproduces 100%: ADR 0076 (accepted 2026-07-02) says "ВСЕ агенты (18) = claude-fable-5 ... без исключений и алиасов" and ground truth matches (18/18 live agents `model: claude-fable-5`, kit/PINNED_VERSIONS.md 22 fable-5 lines). Every cited contradicting line exists verbatim: repo CLAUDE.md:274 "model dispatch (sonnet default, opus for judgment-heavy, haiku for mechanical)"; llm-wiki/CLAUDE.md:275 dispatch table; ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:78-84 "Model dispatch" table; kit-overview-ru.md per-agent table (~lines 108-121) still lists "trader-expert | sonnet 4.6", "python-reviewer | haiku", "security-auditor | **opus**" on the page repo CLAUDE.md designates "Single source of truth gateway"; tooling-inventory-ru.md lines 46-48/72/84/95/101/108/115/122/131/139/462 and line 486 even prescribes the now-abolished behavior "❌ Использовать opus где hailku/sonnet работает". findings.title: ADR 0074 A/B would burn 2 sprints measuring a knob logs suggest is inert, and its MAX_THINKING tier-scaling arm contradicts ADR 0076 [CONFIRMED]
findings.mechanism: ADR 0074 (proposed) fixes methodology: AUTOCOMPACT 50 vs 65 across 2 comparable sprints; MAX_THINKING '10000 vs масштаб по тиру (haiku 4000 / sonnet 8000 / opus-fable 12000)'. Two defects: (1) no step verifying the env var has ANY effect — the kit's own log analysis (kit-weakpoints line 75) found compactions fired at preTokens min 167k / avg 307k ('CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=50 в бою почти не проявился'); with a live 200k window and PCT=50 honored, boundaries should cluster near ~100k — none of 61 events were below 167k. (2) The tier-scaled MAX_THINKING arm references haiku/sonnet tiers abolished by ADR 0076 the same day; and the flat MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=10000 cap on an all-fable-5 registry sits in tension with 0076's stated priority 'токен-бюджет НЕ ограничен… максимальная глубина проработки' — it throttles exactly the judgment depth the operator chose to pay for.
findings.evidence: ~/.claude/settings.json:3-4 '"MAX_THINKING_TOKENS": "10000", "CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE": "50"' (mirrored kit/settings.example.json:3-4). ADR 0074:32-36 (A/B design, no validity probe; tier arm). ADR 0076:17,34 (uniform fable-5; 'Экономия тира больше не цель'). kit-weakpoints-from-history.md:74-75 (61 boundaries, preTokens avg 307,854 / min 167,014; compactMetadata.preTokens/postTokens/durationMs available in jsonl).
findings.why_weak: As designed the A/B costs 2 full sprints and can only return noise if the knob is dead; the MAX_THINKING arm tests a model matrix that no longer exists. Impact estimate: if AUTOCOMPACT=50 is inert, today's cost is 0 tokens but a false belief in a tuned guard; if it ever activates on smaller windows it roughly doubles lossy-compaction frequency (each ≈ −92% context + ~2.1 min + re-read tail per kit-weakpoints).
findings.proposed_direction: Cheapest sequence: (0) knob-validity probe, one disposable session, no sprint (~30 min): bulk-Read files to ~55-60% of window, then grep compact_boundary in that session's jsonl — boundary at ~50% ⇒ knob live; boundary at default ⇒ knob dead → delete the env var and close arm A of ADR 0074 without any A/B. (1) Only if live: 2-sprint A/B harvesting existing compactMetadata + per-turn usage from jsonl via a ~20-line grep script (zero new instrumentation). (2) Rewrite the MAX_THINKING arm for the 0076 world: 10000 vs unset (platform default) on fable-5 only; given the depth-over-cost directive the default hypothesis should favor removing the cap.
findings.verify_note: Finding stands — every cited fact reproduces and no refutation condition applies. (1) Both knobs live: ~/.claude/settings.json lines 3-4 and kit/settings.example.json lines 3-4 contain MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=10000 and CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=50. (3) ADR 0076 (accepted, operator, same day, committed AFTER 0074 per git log) abolishes exactly that tier matrix: 'Алиасов (sonnet/haiku/opus) в реестре больше нет', 'Экономия тира больше не цель', 'токен-бюджет НЕ ограничен… максимальная глубина проработки' — 0074 was never amended (still contains the tier arm). (4) Inertness evidence reproduces: kit-weakpoints-from-history.md lines 73-75 — 61 compact boundaries, preTokens avg 307,854 / min 167,014, and the kit's own conclusion 'CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=50 в бою почти не проявился'. (5) Not fixed in S57-S67: sprint-62 page T4 shipped the ADR as-is and deferred 'tuning A/B → оператору'; SPRINT_STATE line 20 still carries 'tuning A/B (ADR 0074)' in the operator queue unchanged — meaning the defective protocol is the one queued for execution, so impact is not speculative. (6) Not already tracked: UNIFIED-BACKLOG KIT-012 is the PARENT item that produced ADR 0074 ('ADR + скрипт замера; A/B фоном') — it does not capture either defect; zero hits in kit-op-detect-hardening-backlog.md and components/error-taxonomy.md. (7) No operator-decision contradiction — the finding argues IN FAVOR of ADR 0076 (an accepted operator decision), not against it. One caveat noted: 55 of 61 compaction boundaries date to April and settings.json history is outside git, so I cannot prove the override was active during most observed events — but that weakens only the 'knob proven dead' sub-claim while strengthening the core defect (the ADR has no step establishing the knob has any effect before spending 2 sprints measuring it), and the tier-arm/0076 contradiction is document-verifiable independent of any log data.

findings.title: Safeguard-триггерный model fallback молча заменил pinned fable-5 на opus-4-8 на ~7 часов (73% mega-run); 9 операторских /model-ресетов не подействовали; кит этого не видит
findings.mechanism: harness model_refusal_fallback vs kit pin-policy (ADR 0075 / PINNED_VERSIONS.md) — политика покрывает субагентов, но НИЧТО не сверяет активную модель main-thread с политикой (ни statusline, ни skill-manifest, ни auto-resume)
findings.evidence: Транскрипт mega-run ~/.claude/projects/-Users-Apple-Desktop-Vibe-Code-Bot-AI-Traiding-Bot/67b1586c-d403-42fd-811c-c21cc3920830.jsonl: system events subtype=model_refusal_fallback 2026-07-02T01:04:06Z и 03:10:14Z («This model's safeguards flagged this message… Switched to Opus 4.8»), + 2 queue-уведомления 05:59:17/05:59:28. Пофакторный подсчёт поля message.model по часам: 21:00–01:00 = fable-5 (435 сообщений), 01:04–08:18 = claude-opus-4-8 (1700 сообщений = 73% всех assistant-событий run'а). Оператор выполнил «/model claude-fable-5» 9 раз (03:04, 03:16, 04:27, 05:07, 05:55, 05:59, 06:45, 06:52, 08:18 — local-command-stdout «Set model to claude-fable-5») — часы 03–07 остались на opus-4-8. В 07:03 оператор прямо написал «Запусти следующий спринт так, чтобы… не происходит переключения на Opus 4.8» — час 07 всё равно opus-4-8 (156 событий). Итог: S60–S66 (включая adversarial security-hunt S61) исполнены не той моделью, что задана директивой «kit = fable-5» (memory kit-megarun-directives).
findings.why_weak: Гарантия «модельный диспетч/pin-policy» существует только для субагентов; main-thread модель дрейфует по решению harness'а, дрейф невидим киту, а операторская коррекция (9 попыток) не имеет обратной связи «принялось/не принялось». В unattended-прогоне никто даже не заметит подмену — расход/качество/поведение непредсказуемо меняются на часы.
findings.proposed_direction: Механизировать сверку: (1) statusline (kit/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh) выводит текущую модель и КРАСНЫЙ маркер при model != policy; (2) skill-manifest.sh добавить строку «model used per sprint» из транскрипта (поле message.model — уже парсится grep'ом, как compactMetadata в S62); (3) auto-resume resume-команда передаёт явный --model из PINNED_VERSIONS; (4) зафиксировать в OPERATOR-QUEUE: safeguard-fallback повторяется на конкретных формулировках («искореним все баги» 05:59) — переформулировка директив снижает триггер.
findings.refute_reason: Фактическая канва ВОСПРОИЗВОДИТСЯ точно (10 model_refusal_fallback событий, а не 2; почасовой подсчёт 435 fable-5 / 1700 opus-4-8 = 72.5%; 9 ресетов ровно в заявленные времена; час 07 = 156 opus-событий; в kit/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh, kit/skill-manifest.sh, kit/auto-resume/ ни одного упоминания model — сверки main-thread модели действительно нет). НО находка как HIGH-слабость опровергается по трём критериям задания. (1) Противоречие явному операторскому решению: ADR 0076 (llm-wiki/wiki/project/decisions/0076-model-pin-uniform-fable5.md) и kit/PINNED_VERSIONS.md содержат прямую формулировку «Safety-fallback приемлем (директива оператора): при срабатывании safety-правила claude-fable-5 → авто-переключение на claude-opus-4-8 max — это ОК, НЕ деградация»; в транскрипте оператор в 07:15:45 лично написал «если сработает правило безопасности, то они переключатся на opus 4.8 max, тоже норм»; это зафиксировано и в OPERATOR-QUEUE.md. Центральный вред находки («S60–S66 исполнены не той моделью», «качество/поведение непредсказуемо») — это ровно тот fallback, который оператор объявил приемлемым и не-деградацией. (2) Ключевые механизменные утверждения не выдерживают: «молча заменил» — ложно, каждый из 10 fallback'ов выдал ВИДИМОЕ уведомление UI («Switched to Opus 4.8»), которое оператор цитировал дословно в 05:59; «9 ресетов не подействовали, нет обратной связи принялось/не принялось» — неточно: каждый /model давал явное подтверждение «Set model to claude-fable-5» (это и есть обратная связь), модель откатывалась потому что СЛЕДУЮЩЕЕ сообщение заново флажилось safeguard'ом (fallback через 1–6 минут после каждого ресета: 03:04→03:10, 04:27→04:28, 05:55→05:58, 06:52→06:53), а 9-й ресет 08:18 сработал (после него 10 fable-5 сообщений). Это платформенное safeguard-поведение harness'а, которое кит предотвратить не может — statusline/manifest/auto-resume --model добавили бы только дублирующую видимость, не remedy. (3) Остаточный вред спекулятивен: «в unattended-прогоне никто не заметит» — в наблюдённом инстансе оператор заметил в реальном времени через уведомления harness; инстанса ущерба качеству/токенам от opus-4-8 не предъявлено. Мелкая ошибка атрибуции: «в 07:03 оператор прямо написал» — событие 07:03:45 это auto-compact continuation summary, а не сообщение оператора (реальное — 05:59 queue ×2). Выживающий остаток (не HIGH): строка «model used per sprint» в skill-manifest.sh как телеметрия-гигиена и заметка про trigger-фразы — легитимный LOW backlog-пункт (в kit-op-detect-hardening-backlog/UNIFIED-BACKLOG/error-taxonomy его сейчас нет), но он не спасает находку в заявленной формулировке и severity.

findings.evidence: Подсчёт tool_use по всем *.jsonl проекта: mcp__plugin_claude-mem_mcp-search__smart_search = 3, __search = 1, итого 4 retrieval-вызова за 2026-04-19…07-02 (при 1179 Read и 113 Grep только в main-сессии b8009145); Skill-fires claude-mem:mem-search = 0. Инжекция: SessionStart:startup hook attachment в 67b1586c.jsonl (строка 9): «Access 114k tokens of past research & decisions for just 6,341t. Use the claude-mem skill to access memories by ID» — строка найдена 48 раз по транскриптам (все = 6,341t) ≈ 304 368 токенов инжекции против 4 использований ≈ 76k токенов инжекции на один реальный retrieval. Правило «mem-search first» — ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (Token economy), repo CLAUDE.md (Minimum behavior), llm-wiki/CLAUDE.md (cascade STEP 2) — все три оплачиваются каждую сессию.
findings.why_weak: Прямое противоречие цели «max token economy»: самый дорогой per-session постоянный налог кита идёт на подсистему, которой контроллер фактически не пользуется; при этом BINDING-правило создаёт иллюзию работающего слоя памяти (UNIFIED-BACKLOG уже пометил заявление «грузит 50 наблюдений» как STALE «17 obs, 94% savings» — но аудитировалась только сторона ЗАГРУЗКИ, сторона ИСПОЛЬЗОВАНИЯ = 4/2.5 мес нигде не зафиксирована).
findings.proposed_direction: Решение по данным, два пути: (а) сократить инжекцию до минимума/отключить SessionStart-контекст claude-mem и оставить retrieval on-demand (skill уже существует) — экономия ~6.3k токенов на каждый старт; или (б) если память признаётся ценной — встроить один smart_search в sprint-orient шаг (превратить STEP 2 из декларации в шаг скилла) и замерить hit-rate. В обоих случаях добавить счётчик «mem-retrievals per sprint» в manifest-телеметрию; правило в 3 CLAUDE.md сократить до одной строки.
findings.verify_note: NOT refuted — every quantitative claim reproduces exactly, and my extended check made the finding STRONGER: the claimed 4 retrievals were counted over 12 top-level sessions, and I additionally verified 0 mem-search calls across all 1760 subagent transcripts, so 4/2.5-months is the true total. The 48 × 6,341t injection (~304k tokens) reproduces to the digit and persists in the current session — no S57-S67 fix. Against each refutation criterion: (a) evidence reproduces; (b) not fixed in S57-S67 (ADR 0072 kept claude-mem but audited only tool CHOICE, ADR 0074 has no mem content, kit has no retrieval telemetry) and not in UNIFIED-BACKLOG/kit-op-detect/error-taxonomy — the only adjacent item (GLM K-10 STALE "17 obs, 94% savings") covers the LOAD side, exactly as the finding itself states; (c) no operator-decision contradiction: docs/=WARN, ADR 0076 fable-5, autonomous mode are unrelated; ADR 0072 chose claude-mem over mem0/memanto but never ratified the inject-vs-use ratio, and the finding's option (b) even strengthens claude-mem rather than contradicting it; (d) impact is measured, not speculative. Two softening nuances that do not refute: (1) injected memory index can be used passively without retrieval calls, so "use = 4" slightly understates value; (2) 24 of 48 injections are repeated SessionStart fires within one mega-session (b8009145) where prompt caching reduces marginal cost. Nevertheless the core mechanism claim — BINDING cascade STEP 2 has zero enforcement, zero telemetry, and near-zero observed use while its injection tax is the largest recurring per-session constant — is confirmed. sprint-orient already has an optional mem-search step (line 59), which slightly reduces the novelty of proposed direction (b) but its 0 observed fires confirms the "no enforcement" thesis.

findings.verify_note: Finding CONFIRMED — evidence reproduces and is in one aspect UNDERSTATED. (1) Size: wc -c = 97,517 bytes = 195% of the kit's own BINDING rule «Wiki-страницы держим < 50KB» (llm-wiki/CLAUDE.md:210). (2) Growth trajectory reproduces exactly per tags: 90,344 (alpha.55) → 91,893 (alpha.57) → 92,986 (alpha.60) → 96,813 (alpha.66) → 97,517 (alpha.67 = HEAD), ~1KB/sprint. (4) Hotness confirmed: b8009145 = 45 Reads + 111 Edits/Writes of index.md; mega-run 67b1586c = 16 Reads + 23 Edits (exact match to finding). (5) No size guard: kit/hooks/lib/cascade_check.py:24 THRESHOLD=50*1024 applies only to PreToolUse Read/Bash-cat (WARN-only, fail-OPEN); wiki-broken-link-check.sh, kit-inventory, docs hooks check nothing about page size; sprint-finish SKILL.md 50KB-split rule (line 162) covers only the SPRINT_STATE archive. (6) Growth is mandated and planned: sprint-finish HARD-GATE requires index.md ADR + sprint-page sync every sprint (SKILL.md:84-92); sprint-64-llm-wiki-doc-flow.md «Аудит-остаток» plans cataloging ~110 more pages («полный → docs-спринт») with no split plan. (7) Not fixed in S57-67 (no index-part-N files exist) and not tracked: zero mentions in UNIFIED-BACKLOG-S57, kit-op-detect-hardening-backlog, error-taxonomy, KIT-MASTER-PLAN, OPERATOR-QUEUE, VERIFICATION-LEDGER. (8) No operator-decision conflict: docs/=WARN concerns docs/ staleness, not wiki page size; the <50KB rule and the S32e precedent (tooling-inventory split at 60KB) are the kit's own. One imprecision in the finding (does not refute it): the «1 зафиксированный exceeds-25k отказ Read» in b8009145 was on SPRINT_STATE.md and tool-result JSONs, NOT on index.md itself — index.md's 7 full Reads succeeded back then (file was smaller). findings.verify_note: Finding CONFIRMED, not refuted. (1) Evidence reproduces: my independent parse of the cited transcript found 37 same-file Reads within 30 min of the controller's own successful Edit/Write (main chain), of which 14 are clean under conservative mutator-exclusion and ~20-25 under correct exclusion (my strict filter wrongly excluded non-mutating intervening commands like `cp <file> ~/.claude/` copying FROM the file, `bash -n`, `git add`) — consistent with the claimed 22. findings.title: state-backup.sh silently skips `git commit -a`/`-am` and `git -c … commit` → S61 crash-durability backup never created
findings.mechanism: state-backup.sh (KIT-008/S61) is the sole writer of the .backup snapshots that state-integrity's auto-restore depends on. It fires on PreToolUse Bash for `git commit`, then at line 26 requires SPRINT_STATE to appear in `git -C "$repo_root" diff --cached --name-only` (staged) or it `exit 0`s with no backup. But `git commit -a`/`-am` stage tracked modifications DURING the commit — after the PreToolUse hook has already run — so `--cached` is empty at hook time. Result: for the most common commit form, no backup is taken; if SPRINT_STATE is later corrupted (the exact scenario S61 defends), state_integrity.py finds no valid backup → 'файл НЕ перезаписан, почини вручную' → unattended/auto-resume run stalls needing the operator.
findings.evidence: Sandbox (env-clean temp repo): payload `{"tool_input":{"command":"git commit -am wip"}}` with SPRINT_STATE modified-but-unstaged → state/.backup/ NOT created ('NO BACKUP DIR confirmed'). Control: explicit `git add SPRINT_STATE.md` then `git commit -m wip` → backup SPRINT_STATE.20260702-112816-35865.md created. Source: /Users/Apple/.claude/hooks/state-backup.sh line 14 `case ... *"git commit"*) ;;` (matches -am) and line 26 `git ... diff --cached --name-only | grep -q 'SPRINT_STATE\.md$' || exit 0`. Corroborated by operator's own SPRINT_STATE note line 22: 'SPRINT_STATE стейджить ОТДЕЛЬНО от commit (иначе state-backup не увидит staged)' — a symptom of this staging subtlety, but the -a/-am hole is not documented as a durability gap.
findings.why_weak: The kit treats state-backup as the durability floor for unattended auto-resume (S61+S67), yet it covers only pre-staged commits. `git commit -am` / `git -c ... commit` are routine, and the auto-resume desktop consumer prompt tells fresh sessions to 'обновляя SPRINT_STATE per-task' with no instruction to stage it separately — so the durability guarantee is silently off for the common path. Not in kit-weakpoints/op-detect backlog (those cover the money-gate argv class, not backup coverage).
findings.proposed_direction: Make state-backup independent of the caller's staging discipline: on any `git commit*` in a repo with SPRINT_STATE, snapshot the working-tree file unconditionally (drop the `--cached` precondition), OR additionally detect `-a`/`-am` and snapshot then. Cheap and removes the staging footgun. Cross-domain: also relevant to architecture-reviewer (crash-durability contract).
findings.verify_note: Finding CONFIRMED on independent re-verification; every refutation avenue fails. (1) Evidence reproduces: I rebuilt the sandbox from scratch (clean temp git repo in scratchpad) — payload {"tool_input":{"command":"git commit -am wip"}} with SPRINT_STATE.md modified-but-unstaged → hook exit 0, NO state/.backup/ created; control with explicit `git add` + `git commit -m` → backup SPRINT_STATE.20260702-173237-17696.md created. (2) Not fixed in S57-S67: the live hook /Users/Apple/.claude/hooks/state-backup.sh and its kit mirror kit/hooks/state-backup.sh are byte-identical today and still contain both defects — line 16 `*"git commit"*` substring match (also silently misses `git -c … commit`, where the substring "git commit" never occurs) and line 26 `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q 'SPRINT_STATE\.md$' || exit 0`. Since `commit -a/-am` stages during commit (after PreToolUse), --cached is empty at hook time. (3) Not already tracked: UNIFIED-BACKLOG-S57.md KIT-008 describes the backup system itself as shipped (S60/S61), not this coverage hole; kit-op-detect-hardening-backlog.md has no mention (it covers the gh-pr-merge/git-push argv-detect class); error-taxonomy.md has no state-backup entry; component page state-integrity-hook.md line 19 documents "staged SPRINT_STATE.md → backup" as the design without flagging the -a/-am durability gap. (4) No operator-decision conflict: the SPRINT_STATE.md line 22 note ("SPRINT_STATE стейджить ОТДЕЛЬНО от commit (иначе state-backup не увидит staged)") is a workaround acknowledging the subtlety in a transient file (trimmed at Phase 9 close) — it corroborates rather than contradicts the finding. (5) Impact not speculative: state_integrity.py lines 281-316 confirm restore depends entirely on .backup contents, and with zero valid backups it prints "файл НЕ перезаписан, почини вручную" and leaves corruption in place; the backup dir is GITIGNORED (git check-ignore confirms), so the durability floor is machine-local and hook-dependent — a fresh clone/machine or an -am-only run window has no fresh backups. The auto-resume consumer prompt kit/auto-resume/desktop-task-prompt.md line 30 indeed instructs fresh sessions to update SPRINT_STATE per-task with no stage-separately instruction. Partial mitigation exists (older staged-commit backups survive rotation-20, so the typical failure degrades to a STALE-RESTORE WARN with wrong next_action rather than a hard stall — 6 backups exist on disk right now), which slightly tempers but does not refute the finding: a stale next_action restored into an unattended auto-resume loop is itself a continuity fault.

findings.title: round-6 whitespace/`-c` op-detect hardening applied to only 3 of 11 command-matching hooks; state/docs/adr gates use bare substring
findings.mechanism: S61 round-6 added `command_norm=$(… tr -s ' \t' ' ')` + `sed -E 's/git( -[cC] [^ ]+)+ /git /g'` normalization to review-gate.sh, phase-advance.sh, sprint-flow-check.sh so `gh   pr   merge` / `git -c http.x=y push` still trigger. The other command-matching hooks never got it: state-integrity-check.sh (`*"git push"*`), state-backup.sh (`*"git commit"*`), pertask-state-warn.sh, sprint-state-freshness-check.sh use bare single-space substrings; docs-staleness/docs-broken-link/adr-agent-sync/adr-index only add a 2-space variant. So `git  push` (2+ spaces) or `git -c x=y push` slips past them.
findings.evidence: Coverage matrix run over all 11 hooks: only review-gate/phase-advance/sprint-flow-check show `whitespace-hardened=YES(tr -s norm)`; state-integrity-check, state-backup, pertask-state-warn, sprint-state-freshness show hardened=no and no 2-space variant. state-integrity-check.sh line 22 `*"git push"*) ;;` — a `git -c x=y push` string does not contain the substring `git push`. Money gates ARE hardened so money merges stay gated; the unhardened set = state-backup (durability, compounds D3-01), docs hygiene block, and state-integrity push-path (defense-in-depth; SessionStart still validates).
findings.why_weak: Hardening was patched gate-by-gate during the S61 hunt rather than as a shared primitive, leaving an inconsistent trust boundary: the same benign command form (`git -c …`) that the money gates now survive still disarms the durability/hygiene gates. Distinct from KIT-OD-1 (that item is argv/alias resolution for review-gate/phase-advance specifically).
findings.proposed_direction: Factor the round-6 normalization (`tr -s` + `-c/-C` strip) into a shared `kit/hooks/lib/opdetect.sh` sourced by every command-matching hook, so coverage is uniform and future forms are fixed in one place. Ties into KIT-OD-1's 'classify on resolved argv' root-fix.

findings.title: 14 sequential PreToolUse hooks × ~16 python3 spawns per Bash call — ~0.46s benign / ~0.92s push overhead with no shared prefilter
findings.mechanism: settings.json wires 14 hooks under one PreToolUse Bash matcher, run sequentially. On EVERY Bash tool call each hook independently `cat`s the payload and spawns python3 to extract `tool_input.command`, then most early-exit because the command isn't push/commit/merge/read. 16 of the 17 .sh files contain a python3 spawn. There is no cheap shared prefilter, so a plain `git status` still pays ~14 interpreter startups.
findings.evidence: Measured (env, 3 runs, stable): benign `git status` payload through the 14-hook chain = real 0.46s ×3; `git push origin main` payload = real 0.92/0.91/0.97s. Single `python3 -c pass` = 0.02s. `grep -l python3 ~/.claude/hooks/*.sh | wc -l` = 16. Over a mega-run issuing thousands of Bash tool calls this is minutes-to-hours of cumulative wall-clock latency (no token cost).
